report.search_notes:
AG-002 RESEARCH NOTES. Access date for all sources: 2026-10-12.

== METHOD AND LIMITS (read first) ==
- I ran about 30 WebSearch queries: 20 for Task A videos, plus Task B facts and platform guidance.
- Every WebFetch attempt was refused by the proxy: sba.gov (7a, 504, microloans), ecfr.gov, ftc.gov and creators.instagram.com. So NONE of the official pages below were opened directly. Every fact comes from search-result titles and snippets, and the search tool's own summaries, so accessed_via = WebSearch for everything. Confidence is lowered accordingly.
- Before publishing, the operator or QA should open the key official URLs (S01, S03, S06, S08, S10) manually and confirm the figures.

TASK A, VIDEOS:
- Web search indexes mostly TikTok /discover/ and /tag/ pages, not individual videos. Only 9 direct video URLs came up: 6 in scope (V01–V06) and 3 adjacent, real-estate DSCR videos used as format-only references (V07–V09). I did not reach the 15–30 target.
- No direct instagram.com/reel/ URL appeared in any search.
- None of the videos could be opened. No dates, metrics, transcripts or hooks are verified beyond the caption text.
- Video IDs suggest several are 2022–2024, so they are NOT recent.
- I excluded discover/tag pages because they are not video URLs.

== (A) SHORT-FORM FORMAT GUIDANCE ==
The official platform pages could not be opened. Treat every item below as directional only, not as a performance guarantee.
- P1. Instagram's official creators blog page \"Tips for Improving Your Reach\" (https://creators.instagram.com/blog/tips-for-improving-your-reach) appeared in results, but the fetch failed. Search summaries attributed these points to it and other sources:
  - Reels must be 3 minutes or less to be eligible for recommendation.
  - Post original content. Instagram is less likely to recommend reposts or videos with visible watermarks.
  - Confidence: MEDIUM-LOW (the attribution is via a summary).
- P2. Secondary blogs (Hootsuite https://blog.hootsuite.com/instagram-algorithm/ ; OpusClip https://www.opus.pro/blog/instagram-reels-caption-subtitle-best-practices) say:
  - Watch time, likes and sends/shares are key signals, and sends matter more for reaching non-followers.
  - Captions help viewers who watch with sound off.
  - Confidence: LOW to MEDIUM (secondary sources). No engagement figures should be used.
- P3. TikTok. I didn't open an official TikTok page. Secondary sources (https://www.stackmatix.com/blog/tiktok-creative-best-practices-2026 ; https://www.teleprompter.com/blog/tiktok-3-second-rule) attribute the following to TikTok for Business guidance:
  - Introduce the core proposition in the first 3 seconds.
  - Use captions or text overlays for context.
  - Suggested ad length is 21–34 s, but that guidance is for ADS, not organic content.
  - Confidence: LOW. AG-004's brief of 35–60 s organic is a reasonable choice, but no platform source verified an ideal organic length.
- P4. Patterns I saw in the captions found (qualitative only, no performance data):
  - Openers: counter-intuitive insider-truth openers (V01, \"It’s surprisingly tough…\"), 'Reality check:' openers (V04) and expectation resets (V03, \"a longshot, but not impossible\").
  - Formats: '[Jargon] explained' titles (V07); plain-English analogy plus a worked hypothetical number example plus a numbered 'who it's for' list (V09); 'How to [outcome] with an SBA loan' (V05).
  - Endings: comment-prompting questions (V03).
- Anti-patterns to avoid:
  - \"no banks, no hoops\" (V04)
  - \"that’s all the lender needs to know to approve you\" (V09)
  - keyword comment automations (V09)
  - 'link in bio / book a call'
- Unverified claims circulating in TikTok search snippets. DO NOT reuse:
  - \"5-10% down\", \"up to $5M with 10% down and 10 year term\", \"15 to 20% down… prime plus 2%\"
  - \"home equity loans… tax-deductible, easy to qualify\"
  - \"SBA loans… easy to qualify for\"
  - The SBA closing time of \"about 60 days\"

== (B) FACT SHEET ==
Every figure here is subject to change.

KEY CHANGE ALERT:
- Search results from several secondary sources (S11, S12, S13) say SBA SOP 50 10 8.1 took effect on 2026-10-01 and replaced SOP 50 10 8 (in effect since 2025-06-01).
- I couldn't open the official SBA SOP page to confirm the 8.1 text. Cite figures as \"per SBA SOP 50 10 8.1, effective Oct 1, 2026 (subject to change)\" only after the operator confirms.
- FY2027 7(a) fees took effect on 2026-10-01. Don't use FY2026 fee figures.

F1. SBA 7(a) maximum loan amounts (S03, sba.gov lender page \"Types of 7(a) loans\", per snippet):
- Standard 7(a) $5,000,000
- 7(a) Small $350,000
- SBA Express $500,000
- Export Express $500,000
- CAPLines $5,000,000
- International Trade $5,000,000
- EWCP $5,000,000
- Confidence: MEDIUM.

F2. 7(a) guaranty (S03/S04 sba.gov, S05 CRS R41146): generally up to 85% for loans of $150,000 or less, and 75% above $150,000.
- SBA Express guaranty is 50% (per the search summary; the exact sba.gov attribution is unclear).
- International Trade can get up to 90%.
- Confidence: MEDIUM.
- One snippet mentioned past TEMPORARY Express changes ($1M cap, 75% guaranty). Those are historical. Don't use them.

F3. FY2027 7(a) upfront guaranty fee (S01 SBA Information Notice 5000-881797, \"7(a) Fees Effective October 1, 2026 for Fiscal Year 2027\", published Sept 3, 2026, applies to loans approved Oct 1, 2026 to Sept 30, 2027; also S02 NAGGL). For loans over 12 months:
- $150,000 or less: 2% of the guaranteed portion
- $150,001–$700,000: 3%
- $700,001–$5M: 3.5% on the guaranteed portion up to $1M, plus 3.75% above $1M
- Lender annual service fee: 0.55% of the outstanding guaranteed balance. The FY2026 notice says this cannot be charged to the borrower.
- Some rural, manufacturing and food-supply-chain loans get 0% treatment (details not verified).
- Confidence: MEDIUM. Fees change every fiscal year.
- Recommendation: if a script mentions fees at all, describe them qualitatively (\"SBA charges a guaranty fee that varies by loan size and fiscal year\").

F4. Equity injection, startups and changes of ownership (S13 searchfunder / pioneercapitaladvisory on 8.1; S14 starfieldsmith; S18 whitefordlaw on 50 10 8):
- Minimum 10% of total project costs.
- Seller debt on FULL standby can cover no more than half of the required injection, i.e. at least 5% must come from 'unlimited' sources like cash.
- To count, a standby seller note must have NO principal or interest payments for the whole term of the SBA loan.
- Per S13, 8.1 keeps the 10% and half-max structure.
- Confidence: MEDIUM. This came from several consistent secondary sources; I didn't open the SOP itself.
- Wording for scripts: \"generally at least 10% of total project costs under current SBA rules (subject to change).\" Don't say \"10% down guaranteed.\"

F5. Changes under SOP 8.1 (secondary only, LOW-MEDIUM; S11 doeren, S12 sundancefg / jakenfinancegroup). Reported changes:
- Repayment analysis now includes the 2 most recent months of bank statements.
- Change-of-ownership loans no longer use the 7(a) Small Loan path (full underwriting instead).
- A Quality of Earnings report is required for first-time acquisitions or expansions with a purchase price of $3M or more (excluding real estate).
- Change of ownership now sits in Appendix 15.
- Recommendation: AVOID specific 8.1 details until the operator verifies them.

F6. Personal guaranty (S16 security-banks, S18 whitefordlaw; SOP 50 10 8):
- Owners with 20% or more must give a full, unconditional guaranty.
- Anyone who owned 20% or more in the prior 6 months still has to guarantee unless they fully divested.
- Confidence: MEDIUM. I couldn't confirm whether 8.1 changed this.

F7. Ownership and citizenship (S08 SBA Procedural Notice 5000-876626, dated Feb 11, 2026, effective March 1, 2026; S09 GAO B-338157; S10 SBA Policy Notice 5000-876441):
- For 7(a) and 504, 100% of direct and indirect owners must be U.S. citizens or U.S. nationals whose principal residence is in the U.S.
- Lawful permanent residents are no longer eligible owners.
- Confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH (official URL titles plus several consistent sources).
- SENSITIVE. A recent change, and it may be legally contested (the GAO opinion exists). If used, phrase it as \"check current eligibility rules with a lender.\"

F8. SBA Franchise Directory (S15 Taft law bulletin; S17 JD Supra; S16):
- The directory was reinstated with SOP 50 10 8, effective June 1, 2025.
- Per S16, franchisors had to certify by June 30, 2026. Brands that didn't were removed, and their franchisees aren't currently SBA-eligible.
- Confidence: MEDIUM for the reinstatement, LOW-MEDIUM for the certification deadline.
- Script-safe: \"For an SBA loan, lenders generally check whether the franchise brand is on SBA's Franchise Directory.\"

F9. 504 program (S06 sba.gov/loans/504-loans, per snippet): maximum $5.5 million.
- UNVERIFIED nuance: I believe $5.5M applies to certain manufacturing or energy projects, with $5M as the standard cap. Not confirmed.
- Recommendation: omit the figure, or say \"504 loans are for major fixed assets like real estate and equipment.\" Uses and terms were not verified in this session.

F10. Microloans: $50,000 or less (per search summary; the exact source URL is unclear).
- One snippet said they must be repaid within six years. CONFLICT/UNVERIFIED: I couldn't confirm the current maximum term. Omit the term.

F11. FTC Franchise Rule (16 CFR Part 436). No ftc.gov or ecfr page could be opened. From secondary sources (https://nextchapterfranchiseadvisors.com/blog/understanding-the-fdd-what-the-ftc-requires ; https://franchiseinspect.com/glossary/14-day-rule ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franchise_rule):
- The franchisor must give the FDD at least 14 calendar days before the buyer signs a binding agreement or pays money.
- The FDD has 23 items (including fees, estimated initial investment, financing offered, financial performance representations, and franchisee and outlet information).
- Confidence: MEDIUM (long-standing rule, secondary sources only).

NOT VERIFIED, so leave out of scripts:
- 7(a) maximum interest rates
- maturity terms (the common '10 yrs business / 25 yrs real estate' figure was not verified)
- detailed use-of-proceeds lists
- 504 terms and structure
- the Express turnaround time
- credit score minimums (one lender blog cited 650+; not official)
- the 100%-financing rule for same-industry expansion acquisitions (secondary only, and it may have changed under 8.1)
